newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal govt seeks break copper strike deadlock.
newsitem.headline: Portugal govt seeks break copper strike deadlock.

text.p: The government has summoned strike leaders and representatives of the management of the Neves Corvo copper mine to a meeting this evening to try and break a deadlock over working hours, a union leader said on Friday.
Eduardo Lazaro told Reuters that the meeting would be held at the office of the civil governor of Beja, nearby the mine which is located some 250 km southeast of Lisbon.
The meeting, due to start at 1830 GMT, would be attended by representatives of the economy and labour ministries, he added.
The mine, which produces 107,000 tonnes of copper per year, has been paralysed since Monday when miners began an indefinite strike over company plans to introduce Sunday working.
